about: Rules that read hand position, potion-slot position or enemy order (docs/rebuild/FIGHT_SOLVER.md section 2). While a combat holds none of a category's cards (in any pile, queue or screen), the state key uses the canonical form for it: the hand and the potion slots as multisets, equal enemies as interchangeable (StateKey.EnemyClasses). Found by a scan of src/Sts2Emulator (Hand[0], Hand.First/Last, leftmost or first-card helpers, Enemies.First*, PotionSlots[i] reads) on main 08882f79. A card generated into the combat later is scanned when it is in the state: a keyed node decides its forms from what it holds. The equal-value harness (S3) checks the canonical forms on positions with and without readers.

cards.name: Acrobatics
cards.why: its generated-card form discards the first card of the hand (DiscardFirstCardsFromHand)

cards.name: Reboot
cards.why: its generated-card form walks the hand from the first card

cards.name: CalculatedGamble
cards.why: discards the hand from the first card: per-card discard triggers fire in hand order

cards.name: Eidolon
cards.why: exhausts from the first card of the hand (ExhaustFirstCardsFromHand)

cards.name: FiendFire
cards.why: exhausts the hand from Hand[0]: per-card exhaust triggers fire in hand order

potion_slot.why: the scan found no rule that reads a potion's slot index beyond the action's own slot argument

enemy_order.why: acting order is slot order, and an untargeted effect takes the first targetable enemy (CombatEngine's default target, CardEffects' FirstOrDefault(IsTargetable) sites): every combat has a reader until the S3 harness shows which positions do not, so EnemyClasses keeps every enemy distinct
